title: First Rain, First Leak: How East Bay Landlords Should Triage Winter Repair Calls

findings.quote: the repair clock starts when you get notice
findings.root_cause: Civil Code 1942(a) is specific to notice of untenantable conditions; phrasing sweeps in all reports.
findings.fix: Replace 'the repair clock starts when you get notice' with 'Once you receive notice of a condition affecting habitability, respond within a reasonable time for the circumstances; document and investigate every leak report.'
findings.future_prevention: Apply the same correction to parent article, video page, and script; verify before publication.

findings.root_cause: Operational emergency classification is not by itself a legal determination that emergency entry is warranted.
findings.fix: Replace 'Emergency entry without notice (§1954)' with 'Emergency entry without advance notice only where circumstances constitute an actual emergency under §1954; otherwise use statutory notice or applicable consent.'
findings.future_prevention: Apply the same correction to parent article, video page, and script; verify before publication.

findings.quote: Two kinds of calls should always move up a tier: anything involving electrical, and anything where the tenant mentions a musty smell or spots on the wall.
findings.root_cause: Musty odor and stains call for prompt investigation but aren't necessarily legally defined emergencies.
findings.fix: Replace with 'Treat water near electrical fixtures as a potential immediate safety hazard. Prioritize prompt inspection of musty odors or suspected mold, and escalate based on the actual risk.'
findings.future_prevention: Apply the same correction to parent article, video page, and script; verify before publication.

findings.quote: Watch the video version, with chapter links and a full transcript.

findings.future_prevention: Apply the same correction to parent article, video page, and script; verify before publication.
